clue.text: Attack in which sergeant-major captures rocky hill

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the sergeant-major's letters enclose the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A battle scene in which a sergeant-major leads troops to seize a craggy hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it in a sudden assault, so the noun is a military onslaught.

clue.text: Precious stones beneath rock layers in plots

indicators.note: in a down answer, the stones come below the rock layers

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
gems are precious stones

explanation.surface: Jewels lie buried under layers of rock in plots of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' looks like plots of ground in the geological picture; it means schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratagems are cunning schemes or ruses devised to outwit someone.

clue.text: Strange characters picked up in Buckland Down

indicators.note: in a down answer, picked up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards
in means the letters are found within the place name

explanation.surface: Odd folk spotted around a Dorset downland village.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters DDO lie inside 'BucklanD DOwn' and 'picked up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd is a common synonym for strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Substance found in mass on Dart

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a dart is a small arrow

explanation.surface: Material found in a great quantity on the River Dart in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D makes 'Dart' look like the Devon river; it is a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrow can mean the essential core or substance of something, as in the marrow of an argument.

clue.text: Such radio stations apparently incompatible with 11?

definitions.meaning: radio stations broadcasting on a band of high-frequency signals that travel far
11 across is THE LONG GOODBYE; a wave is a goodbye, and short is the opposite of long, so a brief wave cannot be a long farewell

explanation.surface: A puzzled note that some radio broadcasters seem at odds with another entry in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is playful: read as two words, a short wave is a quick farewell gesture, the contrary of a long goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortwave is the high-frequency broadcasting band used by international radio services.

clue.text: Massacre earl's thug arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A slaughter organised by an aristocrat's hired heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter and massacre both mean the brutal killing of many people.

clue.text: Best garden party?

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to beat them, a verb
read as two words, an ... is a party held outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is a verb here, not the superlative. The second half splits the word: a do is a party, and one in the garden is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo a rival is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: Dither insanely about a good period for retirement activity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the pair
insanely means wildly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pensioners wavering crazily over a fine time to take up a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insanely' turns DITHER into THIRDE, and 'about' puts AG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the active years after retirement, following youth and working life.

clue.text: Problems aired here — such as pain associated with spine?

parts.note: agony is intense pain
the spinal column is the spine

explanation.surface: A newspaper page for troubles, like backache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such as pain associated with spine' hints at back pain, but the two words just join.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper feature in which readers' personal problems are published and answered.

clue.text: Language Beardsley uses occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, here every second one

explanation.surface: The illustrator Aubrey Beardsley now and then uses a particular tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic of Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Bird having resources — tail first — to break perch

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the moved word sits within the perch

parts.note: a perch is a rest for a bird

indicators.note: the last letter is brought to the front of the word for resources

parts.note: bread is slang for money, i.e. resources

explanation.surface: A bird with funds swoops down backwards onto a perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resources' is slang money here; 'tail first' yields DBREA, which 'to break' sets inside the perch.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin redbreast is the familiar name for the European robin, a garden songbird.

clue.text: Jeremy the player for certain clubs

definitions.meaning: the actor Jeremy ..., a player on stage and screen
golf clubs with angled metal heads, numbered three to nine

explanation.surface: A man called Jeremy plays for particular sports clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sportsman, but here it means an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is an English actor, and a set of golf clubs includes several metal-headed ones by that name.

clue.text: Ode by Gogol then adapted for book and film

indicators.note: a work adapted is reshaped, so these letters are rearranged into a new title

explanation.surface: A poem by the Russian writer Gogol is turned into a novel and then a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' fits the screen-adaptation picture but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler's Philip Marlowe novel of 1953 was made into a Robert Altman movie in 1973.

clue.text: Frantically get appeal in for first offence?

indicators.note: frantically means wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A desperate bid to lodge an appeal after a first conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Eve eating the forbidden fruit in Eden, the first sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The forbidden fruit eaten by Eve was traditionally an apple, the original sin of Genesis.

clue.text: Combine with two sailors in an investment producing capital

parts.note: to add is to combine

indicators.note: in means the sailors are placed within the investment

parts.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a UK tax-free savings scheme

indicators.note: two means the abbreviation for sailor appears twice

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: Merge with a couple of seamen in a scheme yielding funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in this financial surface; it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Gloomy music fan acquired heroin

parts.note: acquired means got
H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A miserable music lover has obtained drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Goths follow a dark-styled rock subculture, dressing in black and favouring melancholy music.

clue.text: Keep firm grasp in wrestling

parts.note: firm means strong, solid
a hold is a wrestler's grip on an opponent

explanation.surface: Maintain a solid grip during a wrestling bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: the central tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's keep is its fortified inner tower, a fortress within the walls.

clue.text: Girl having paddle round saw manor demolished

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman wields a paddle while a mansion is torn down.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rower is one who propels a boat with an oar, a kind of paddle.

clue.text: Cheeky little devil — pupil chucking stone

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: chucking means throwing away, so the stone abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: a student is a pupil
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A naughty child, a schoolboy throwing rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent means insolent or disrespectful, much like saucy.

clue.text: In Paris my new term involves painting here?

definitions.text: In Paris my new term involves painting here?

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold, so the reworked letters wrap around the art
new signals that the letters of term are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: A student in Paris starts a new term studying painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives TMRE and 'involves' wraps it round the painting. The whole clue doubles as the definition, since this hill district was home to painters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hilltop quarter of northern Paris famous for artists such as Picasso and Toulouse-Lautrec.

clue.text: Volcano initially falling under Jovian influence

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A mountain coming under the sway of Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest peak, a dormant stratovolcano near Tokyo.

clue.text: Places echo after shell goes off in coup

parts.note: places means puts

indicators.note: losing its shell means the outer letters of the word go, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Gunfire echoes around as shells explode during a military takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' here belongs with the indicator: the inner letters of ECHO come after PUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is an attempt to overthrow a government, as in Hitler's Munich bid of 1923.

clue.text: Country dad eats acceptable fowl with mint

indicators.note: to eat is to take inside, so the word for dad swallows the letter

parts.note: papa is another word for dad
U means acceptable, as in U and non-U (upper-class usage)
mint condition means new
a guinea fowl, shortened to guinea

explanation.surface: Father eats a nice bird dish flavoured with mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts the U inside the word for dad. 'mint' looks like the herb, but means unused, as in mint condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Papua New Guinea is a nation occupying the eastern half of the island of New Guinea.

clue.text: Retreat to north to cover country devastatingly attacked

indicators.note: covering something means going around it, so the reversed retreat wraps the country
in a down answer, going north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A northern withdrawal to shield a nation under heavy assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to north' reverses the retreat to NED, and 'to cover' wraps that round the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To nuke a place is to attack it with nuclear weapons, or devastate it utterly.

clue.text: Swamp creature caught by enormous bird

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A crocodile seized by a huge bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is short for crocodile, a reptile found in swamps and rivers.

clue.text: Pity about Europe wasting its money, some in India

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for pity goes around what is left

parts.note: rue means regret or pity

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the currency letters are removed from the continent

parts.note: the euro is the currency of much of Europe

explanation.surface: A lament over Europe squandering its cash, part of which goes to India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' leaves PE from the continent once its currency goes, and 'about' sets the pity word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian currency unit, so 'some' money as spent in India.

clue.text: Article on a smart UK foreign relations manual

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it
foreign suggests something strange and altered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news article about a clever British guide to international diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign relations' reads as diplomacy, but 'foreign' is the anagram signal and 'relations' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Sanskrit text is famous as a guide to love and sexual relations.

clue.text: Potentially poisonous creature dispenses with a fox

indicators.note: dispensing with something means doing without it, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: some toads secrete toxins from their skin

explanation.surface: A dangerous animal does away with a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: Tod is a Scottish and northern English word for a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Tod is a dialect name for the fox, as in Beatrix Potter's Mr Tod.

clue.text: Deceived in trick getting furious inside

indicators.note: inside means the angry word goes within the trick

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
heated means furious, angry

explanation.surface: Someone duped by a swindle becomes enraged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheated on is to be betrayed or deceived, especially by an unfaithful partner.

clue.text: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour

definitions.text: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour

parts.words: One renewed after cuts put an end to by Labour
parts.note: a many-headed serpent whose heads grew back when severed, killed by Hercules as one of his twelve Labours

explanation.surface: Something revived after spending cuts, then finished off by the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' and 'Labour' suggest British politics; Labour is really one of the tasks of Hercules.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Lernaean monster regrew two heads for each one cut off until Hercules slew it.
